steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease two cookie sheets.
Stir flour, baking soda, and salt together in a small bowl.
Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a bowl with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy.
Stir in peanut butter, egg, and vanilla until well blended.
Mix in flour mixture until just moistened. Stir in chocolate chips and oats until evenly distributed.
Drop tablespoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges start to brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: I just made these as written & they are WONDERFUL!!! My favorite part about this cookie is it's texture. Like others have said, they don't spread- which is a MUST in my book! 10 minutes is perfect. Be sure to mix the sugars, butter, PB, egg, & vanilla first- then add the flour mixed with the soda, salt, & oats. Lastly the ch chips. Amazing cookie- thanks so much for submitting!

Love these cookies but I do a couple things a bit differently. I start by browning my butter and letting it set back up. I switch the sugar ratios by using 1/2cup of brown sugar and 1/3cup of white. I toast my oatmeal and sometimes add half toasted coconut/half toasted oatmeal but not always. finally, I do add a bit more vanilla in paste form and more peanut butter followed by chilling them in the fridge for 2 hours before baking. Fantastic cookies as is but phenomenal by doing a bit more work.

This is my favorite chocolate chip cookie I have ever found and I have been baking for over 50 years! The only alteration I did was use large dark chocolate chips. I prefer the taste of chocolate over sugar. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. I make 12 to 14 large cookies and bake 14 minutes exactly. I take them out and leave them to finish baking 5 minutes on the cookie sheet. This makes them nicely chewy from the oatmeal. And the cookie takes longer to eat and enjoy. Really delicious and a great combination in this recipe. The majority love this recipe and there is a reason. It is the best Chocolate Chip Cookie ever!

I have made these several times to rave reviews. One time, I even ran out of chocolate chips and made a batch without them and they were still delicious. Some things I do: whip the first two steps each time until fluffy, but only mix dry ingredients until incorporated being sure to not over mix. I also refrigerate the dough for at least half an hour before scooping onto the pan. This helps the cookies stay thicker. I found the dark chocolate chips were preferred to semi-sweet.

These cookies are FANTASTIC and ALL of my family members are chocolate cookie lovers AND critics! These are by far the most amazing and have excellent flavor and texture. Two tricks learned from my elders: 1) Add 1/4-1/2 cup of flour at the very end, helps make cookies bigger/fluffier. 2) Cook at only 325 degrees instead of 350 and remove from the oven 2-3 minutes early and let them continue to bake on the tray. 

This house full of cookie lovers rates these TOP NOTCH!

Pure yumminess! So I made the recipe exactly as stated and my friends loved them! I personally am not much of a PB fan, so I made it again, this time tweaking the PB (added 1/4 Cup since I doubled the recipe) and can't get enough. I also did add a tsp of cinnamon. I am a cookie snob and these cookies have the best of all 3 worlds, oatmeal, PB and c.chips.

I love this recipe! I made it gluten-free by swapping the wheat flour for Bob's Red mill 1-for-1, and they still came out great! I also used crunchy peanut butter since I was making them for nut-lovers, and they are a huge hit.
I made this for my family and they loved them. Added 1/2 cup of macadamia nuts and that went well, and for another batch put a 1/2 of a candied cherry on top. This is a really great flexible recipe!

Simply delicious! Hubby and daughter suggested turning up the PB, so on second batch I increased it (added another 1/3cup). Also swapped the white and brown sugar measurements, based in other review. My new go-to cookie!
I doubled the recipe because I’m gifting them. I used half creamy half crunchy peanut butter, 1C semi sweet and 1C Reese’s peanut butter chips! To die for!! 🩷

These cookies were like drugs. Didn't want to stop eating them. :-) I added some coconut and chopped pecans and was a little more liberal with the peanut butter. Also doubled the recipe and used the mini chocolate chips. One of my family's favorites!
Easy, delicious, not too peanut buttery! They were perfect!

Absolutely awesome! So easy to follow, easy to make (I recommend using more of a 1/4 cup of oats) to still have that "oat-y" flavor but not "oatmeal chocolate chip cookies" that's a different story! Thank you for this recipie!
All ingredients at room temperature helps for easy mixing.
Loved the recipe, made it exactly per the directions and family Loved them. Was also a good recipe to test out my new hand held mixer on.

i absolutely LOVE this recipe! i have made them so many times and everytime they come out tasting amazing! they are just so melt in your mouth soft and have just the right amount of chocolate and peanut butter. one of the best cookie recipes ever 😋😋😋
These are my go-to cookie every time. I add more Chocolate chips, some walnuts and sometimes dried cherries. They freeze great.

I have dubbed these "The Everything Cookie". My husband doesn't like oatmeal cookies, or peanut butter cookies, but he says these are, "Tasty!" High praise! I have made them sooo many times and it is ALWAYS a crowd-pleaser! Most are skeptical to begin with but completely won over after the first bite. Most recently, a friend told me she doesn't like chocolate chip cookies but she would give it a try because I made them. I just waited... as soon as she tried it she couldn't stop exclaiming about how delicious they were, even with the chocolate chips!! I think one of the best things about this recipe is how adaptable it is. I am trying to reduce sugar and have cut the sugar in half, they are still scrumptious and perhaps even more dunkable in milk or coffee! If I run out of vanilla extract, I have substituted hazelnut extract (enhances the chocolate flavor), rum extract (yummm!) and almond extract (which adds a cherry flavor I LOVE, but no one else seems to notice). I have made it with half the chocolate chips... it's just a nearly indestructible cookie! Because of that I think it would be a great cookie to get someone started baking. : ) Thank you for sharing this recipe, Joan!

This is my Go To cookie recipe!! I like to make GF so I use 1/2 c almond flour + 3/4 c GF flour or 1/2 c of each plus a bit extra to get right texture. Other adjustments: I cut white sugar to 1/4c and brown sugar to 1/3c altho recipe calls for 1/2 c. I added extra 1/4-1/3 c oatmeal. I usually use dark choc chips. I added coarsely chopped almonds bc I 🩷 nuts. I used a small icecream scoop onto a silicone mat on cookie sheet. Baked for 10-12 mins. I’ve made with reg flour and almond. The almond flour cookies are definitely moister.
